questions.question: A cake is cut into 8 equal slices. 2 are sold in the morning and 3 in the afternoon. What fraction is sold, what fraction is left, and how do you know?
questions.expected_answer: 2/8 plus 3/8 is 5/8 sold: add the tops and keep the eighths. The whole cake is 8/8, so 3/8 is left.

questions.question: 40 visitors chose cakes 15, sweets 10, games 9 and crafts 6. Check the total, find how many more chose cakes than crafts, and write one prediction.
questions.expected_answer: 15 plus 10 plus 9 plus 6 is 40, matching the visitors. Cakes beat crafts by 15 minus 6, which is 9. Prediction: next year the cake stall will probably be the busiest again.

questions.question: Write 2 kg 30 g in grams, find the mass of 6 bags of 250 g, and say whether circles tessellate.
questions.expected_answer: 2 kg 30 g is 2 030 g. 6 times 250 g is 1 500 g, which is one and a half kilograms. Circles do not tessellate, because they leave gaps when packed together.
